picks.title: Google rolls back the needless AI generation tools it added to Google Earth
picks.excerpt: Days after adding its Nano Banana generative-image tools to Google Earth, Google is pulling them back following user backlash that AI-invented renderings degraded a trusted mapping/visualization product. A concrete signal on the limits of dropping generative image AI into spatial-design and place-based visualization workflows.
picks.rationale: A hard reversal after backlash — the strongest actionable signal on where generative image AI does and doesn't belong in spatial/place-based design; a genuine follow-up to the launch already covered, distinct URL and event.

picks.title: Rebelle 8.3 proves the future of digital painting isn't AI, it's making brushes feel real
picks.excerpt: Escape Motions' Rebelle 8.3 doubles down on physically realistic brush and watercolor simulation rather than generative AI, framing a deliberate craft-first counter-position in a design-tool market racing to bolt on AI. A useful read on where creative software is choosing simulation over generation.
picks.rationale: A concrete tool release staking a simulation-over-generation position — a credible craft-first counterpoint for tool choices; second render card, given a distinct accent (#7928ca).

picks.title: Jakob's Law: how to apply it as AI collapses surfaces into one chat box
picks.excerpt: As AI collapses distinct app surfaces and screens into a single conversational chat box, this piece reworks Jakob's Law of familiarity for generative UI - what patterns designers must preserve so users still feel oriented when the interface itself is generated on the fly.
picks.rationale: Reworks a foundational UX law for generative UI — directly changes how designers preserve orientation when interfaces are generated on the fly.

picks.title: Rethinking friction in an AI world
picks.excerpt: A designer's argument that 'frictionless' is the wrong default once AI can do almost anything instantly - reframing where intentional friction should be added back into AI-driven products to keep users in control, and how that reshapes the design process.
picks.rationale: Challenges the frictionless default and argues where to add intentional friction back into AI products — an actionable reframe for everyday product-design decisions.
